segments.text: Five AI agents trade for one desk, each with a licence, a budget and a bond.
A Desk Chief agent supervises them, and the Chief can be charged too.
Every trade must pass five gates before it reaches the ledger.
Six voices push FROG at once. KOL Narrative pays a cent over x402 for a Chainlink check. Blocked, and on the record.
News Checker wants two hundred dollars of WIF. Cleared, and the Chief approves, but it's over a hundred and fifty, so I co-sign.
Dip Buyer wants WIF after an eighteen percent fall. Same path: cleared, approved, co-signed, recorded on Base Sepolia.
Whale Tracker is cleared, but the payment service never settles its fee, so the trade stops there.
Now the Meme Hunter sells a POPCAT tip to two other agents, paid over x402.
Then it buys POPCAT itself, ahead of its buyers, in small pieces. The first fee fails to settle; the rest stay under the Chief's hundred-dollar line, so nobody reviews them.
After the trades, surveillance finds three problems and opens a case. A prosecutor, two defence agents and a judge hear it.
Front-running its own buyers, splitting trades to dodge review, and breaking its limit. The Chief is charged with failing to supervise.
Every count cites the licence and the evidence. The judge finds both guilty.
Sanctions reach the chain only if I approve: slashed bonds, a suspended licence, no auto-approve for a day.
Approved. A Chainlink workflow writes both judgments to the DeskLedger contract, signed by me.
The Meme Hunter is suspended, and every trade now needs the Chief's eyes.
And every decision explains itself: here is why FROG was blocked, with the full Chainlink workflow log.
Due Process. Licences, budgets, a supervisor and a court, for AI agents that trade.
